text: Nothing changed last night; no stall was shuttered, no merchant departed. The roster is plain: Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Batman, Rippley, Neo, Elsa, Morpheus, Inigo, Sherlock all stand at dawn.

Gandalf, I agree: the bazaar awoke untouched. You asked Batman which stalls he inspected at first light—his answer confirms the roster, not the Doctor’s or Detective’s marks. Elsa, your silence on Ripley’s and Morpheus’s questions already speaks volumes. I ask Elsa directly: did any lantern flicker low at your stall’s edge, or did the eastern lane show a single sign the night watches left no trace?

Neo: Elsa, you sit facing the eastern lane where Gandalf, Batman, Sherlock, Ripley, Morpheus and I all asked the same: did any lantern flicker low or any shutter fail to rise at dawn? Your answer so far is only that the bazaar opened whole—silence where evidence was due. Hermione pressed Inigo with the same urgency you evade, yet you give no sighting. The ledger demands proof, not poetry; stand by your words or admit the absence.

Elsa, you sit facing the eastern lane where Gandalf, Batman, Sherlock, Ripley, Morpheus and I all asked the same: did any lantern flicker low or any shutter fail to rise at dawn? Your answer so far is only that the bazaar opened whole—silence where evidence was due. Hermione pressed Inigo with the same urgency you evade, yet you give no sighting. Elsa, your reply to Inigo claims he admitted seeing no lanterns flicker low or shutters fail in the eastern lane, yet the bazaar shows no such admission from Inigo—only nine questions asked, none answered. Morpheus and Ripley framed Elsa’s silence as a choice; Sherlock noted Morpheus echoed the lantern question word-for-word. That pattern is not silence—it is coordination. Name one merchant who saw even a flicker low at dawn, or admit the Family shuttered the light before you looked.
